created_at_policy: Use the actual file creation time and execution timestamps in the source manifest; no assumed wall-clock time.
purpose: Respond to the explicit request for individual beam and floor resistance by assembling an executable, labelled component model for impact-zone Floors 93-99. This is a structural prototype, not a complete as-built building model or a new collapse verdict.
scope_adjustment: The user's component-resistance request takes priority in V11A. The previously recorded V10Y initial-drop time, missing half-floor mass and terminal energy corrections remain mandatory before global coupling and are not silently declared fixed.
baseline_damage_policy: All component calculations use an intact idealized baseline; no impact damage, connection removal or member-temperature history is assigned by this iteration.

core_beam_law.fy_source: NIST model material ID 2, reused from V8H; every beam section assignment remains hypothetical
core_beam_law.limits: Ideal in-plane flexure and web shear; no lateral torsional buckling, eccentricity, connection bolt/weld mechanics or load interaction. Connection factors and fracture rotation are hypotheses.

column_law.story_convention: Segment F-to-F+1 uses the section assigned at F by the V8B band convention: F<=94:95-92; F95-97:98-95; F>=98:101-98. Actual splice offsets within stories unresolved.
column_law.status: V8B nominal flexural-buckling screening curve, not an allowable load or certified fire design capacity; local plate, torsional, connection and splice failures not checked

floor_bay.reference: NIST NCSTAR 1-6C pp69-70, C32T1, one of two trusses at exterior Column143 Floor96; not the schedule of every bay
floor_bay.short_span_status: 433 in is reused from V8M; applying C32T1 sections to it is an explicit extrapolation, not a short-truss transcription
floor_bay.depth_status: 29 in is the diagram dimension, used as an approximate chord-node separation; true centroid offsets and bearing offsets unresolved
floor_bay.slab_thickness_note: Detailed 1-6C p69 gives 4.35 in; overview 1-6 p85 rounds to 4.3 in. Neither is the 4 in topping thickness alone.
floor_bay.web_diameter_assignment_status: The source reports both diameters, mostly 1.09 in, but not each bar assignment here; uniform diameter cases are bounds
floor_bay.panel_topology_status: Ideal pin-jointed Warren truss with top nodes at supports, uniformly spaced top panels and staggered bottom nodes. Panel counts and end geometry are hypotheses, not digitized construction details; this is layout sensitivity, not mesh convergence.
floor_bay.truss_yield_strength_status: Explicit grade bounds pending individual steel assignment; not inferred from the core-beam material ID
floor_bay.load_status: Published approximate dead+service live reference; includes floor self-weight, so no extra dead load is added
floor_bay.support_boundary: Left top node pinned, right top node vertical roller; no support shortening or imposed horizontal restraint
floor_bay.cross_section_status: Two opposed rectangular L shapes, no fillets, angle gap set to the selected web diameter; local and torsional buckling not solved

concrete_hypotheses.status: Uncalibrated sensitivity assumptions, not NIST material tables
concrete_hypotheses.ideal_mode_rule: Add Ec*Ac to the top-chord axial stiffness only; perfect bond, compressive slab force sharing, fully braced steel top chord. No slab bending, tension, deck, reinforcement, punching or knuckle failure capacity credited. Reject this branch if any loaded top chord is in tension.

floor_bay.steel_temperature_use: Uniform prescribed temperature changes E and strength; thermal expansion, gradients, creep and fire history are not solved
floor_bay.limit_rule: Solve elastic equilibrium, then report the first nominal member or seat limit under proportional gravity loading. No post-limit continuation; compression bars use min(A*Fy, Euler), an ideal upper screening bound, not a nonlinear buckling solution.
floor_bay.seat_rule: Compare twice the single-truss reaction with complete paired-seat table values. Sweep all 7 interior x 8 exterior details; no as-built detail assignment. Horizontal capacities are exported but not activated by the roller model.

new_source_transcription.source: NIST NCSTAR1-6 Table4-5, PDF158 printed76, visually checked 2026-09-05
new_source_transcription.interaction_warning: Vertical and horizontal values are different loading modes; no validated combined V-H failure surface or ductility law is inferred.

bounded_pdf_review.question: Verify the published seat capacities, paired tributary width, span, slab and chord dimensions of the floor-truss example.
Verify truss chord separation and the representative finite-element topology; do not infer an all-floor member schedule from this example.

model_limits: Individual core-column schedules are archival manual transcriptions, still awaiting an independent second pass.
Historical AISC section properties are edition proxies and core coordinates are approximate reconstructions.
Core beam topology beyond the documented moment-beam subset and every beam-section assignment remain hypotheses.
Use a representative floor bay, not an invented complete floor-truss count or a capacity sum over overlapping tributary areas.
Temperature cases are prescribed steel temperatures, not a fire calculation or a member temperature history.
No global resistance energy is inferred by summing member force capacities.
No new Blender collapse trajectory or historical collapse conclusion is authorized by this iteration.
